Classes

Physics

Why does a bigger jump send you farther? Why does a wider line through a berm carry more speed? Where does your speed go when you brake? Start with the ride, make a prediction, then find the physics that explains it.

2 courses · 9 units · 28 modules · 2 flagship labs live, 21 on the way

Modelled on Carnegie Mellon University’s Open Learning Initiative College Physics 1 and 2.

The route

Two courses, ride them in order. Every module starts from a riding question. Modules with a ▸ lab have an interactive lab you can use today; their full lessons are being written. Log in and your progress shows on every module.

Course 1 · Start here

Trail Physics

Mechanics & Energy

The mechanics of riding: motion, jumps, forces and cornering, energy and momentum, then rotation, fluids, suspension, waves and heat.

6 units · 17 modules · 3 labs ready

  1. Unit 1 Physics Foundations

    What physics is, the maths it runs on, and how to measure the world honestly.

    1. Module 1

      Introduction to Physics

      What’s actually happening, physically, when you ride a bike down a trail?

      Lesson coming

    2. Module 2

      Mathematics Review

      How steep is that climb, really?

      ▸ Berm LabLesson coming

    3. Module 3

      Scientific Measurement

      Your GPS says 38 km/h. A timing gate says 35. Which one do you trust?

      ▸ Berm LabLesson coming

  2. Unit 2 Understanding Motion

    Describe motion in one and two dimensions, from a rider on a straight trail to a rider in the air.

    1. Module 4

      Motion in One Dimension

      Lesson coming

    2. Module 5

      Vectors

      Ride 30 m east and then 40 m north. How far are you from where you started?

      Lesson coming

      Projectile Motion

      Newton’s Laws of Motion

    2. Module 8

      Friction, Slopes and Springs

    3. Module 9

      Uniform Circular Motion

      ▸ Berm LabLesson coming

  4. Unit 4 Energy & Momentum

    Energy, work, power and momentum: the bookkeeping of a ride.

    1. Module 10

      Energy and Gravitation

      Where does your speed come from when you drop into a descent?

      Lesson coming

    2. Module 11

      Work and Power

      Momentum and Collisions

  5. Unit 5 Bike Mechanics

      Rotational Dynamics

      Waves

      What makes a bike buzz, rattle and hum on a rough trail?

    2. Module 17

      Thermodynamics

      Where does all your speed go when you brake down a long descent?

      Lesson coming

Course 2 · Advanced enrichment

Trail Technology

Electricity, Magnetism & Optics

The physics inside modern bike technology: e-bike motors and batteries, circuits and lights, sensors and wireless, lenses and light.

3 units · 11 modules · labs in development

  1. Unit 7 Electricity

    Charge, voltage, current, resistance and circuits, through e-bike batteries and bike lights.

    1. Module 1

      Introduction: The Electric Bike

      What turns a battery’s charge into a push up the climb?

      Lesson coming

    2. Module 2

      Electric Charge and Electric Field

      Why does a jacket crackle when you pull it off after a cold, dry ride?

      Lesson coming

    3. Module 3

      Electric Potential and Capacitors

      What does the 36 V on an e-bike battery actually mean?

      Lesson coming

    4. Module 4

      Current, Resistance and Ohm’s Law

      Why does a brighter bike light drain its battery faster?

      Lesson coming

    5. Module 5

      Circuits and DC Instruments

      If you wire two lights to one battery, does it matter how?

  2. Unit 8 Magnetism & Wireless Technology

    Magnetic fields, motors and generators, and the electromagnetic waves behind GPS and wireless sensors.

      Magnetism

      How does a magnet on a spoke tell your bike computer how fast you’re going?

      Electromagnetic Induction

      Electromagnetic Waves

      Geometric Optics

How every module works

  1. 1HookStart with a riding question, not an equation.
  2. 2PredictSay what you think will happen before you find out.
  3. 3LearnThe physics, its vocabulary and equations, in short sections.
  4. 4ExperimentChange the variables in a lab and watch what happens.
  5. 5CalculateWorked riding problems: knowns, unknown, equation, units, meaning.
  6. 6ChallengeA concept question, a maths problem and a simulation challenge.
  7. 7ExplainClaim, evidence, reasoning: say what you found and why.

Three ways in

  • Explore Visual explanations, demonstrations and guided predictions, with minimal equations.
  • Apply Algebra, unit conversions, graphs and multi-step problems: standard high school physics.
  • Engineer Multi-variable models, trigonometry, uncertainty, model assumptions and independent investigations.

Students can work at different levels within the same module, so a strong rider who’s still building their math can take on the same physics as an advanced student.

Progress

  • Not started No questions answered on this module’s skills yet.
  • In progress Some of the module’s skills practised.
  • Practised Every skill in the module practised.
  • Mastered Every skill practised, and at least 80% of your most recent first tries on each one right. Opening a page or watching an animation never counts. Come back any time: newer work replaces older.
